method: Read README, repository tree and selected source/tests/results at exact main commit SHAs. No tests were executed in this audit.

records.name: synergy_agent_long_term_memory
records.scope: README and complete repository tree
findings: README contains only a title; repository tree contains only README.md.
No implementation, tests, API or executable memory capability established.

records.name: synergy_ai_browser-
records.scope: README, browser runtime and core tests
findings: Top-level document navigation is restricted to HTTPS allowlisted hosts; embedded credentials, direct IP and nonstandard ports are rejected.
Actions are limited to click/fill/press; arbitrary agent-supplied JavaScript is rejected.
Tests cover unsafe top-level URLs, local opt-in, local DOM interaction and detector result parsing.

SECURITY FINDING: _guard_request applies NavigationPolicy only to navigation requests with resource_type=document; all subresource requests are continued without equivalent host/IP checks. An allowlisted page may attempt private-network requests unless network isolation blocks them.

records.name: tiimeweb_synergy_exactly_once_delivery
records.scope: README, SQLite experiment and invariant tests
findings: Robust path uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE, unique event_id, SHA-256 payload fingerprint and effect insert in one SQLite transaction.
Crash probes exercise process exit before and after commit, then repeated redelivery.
README states CI checks syntax and minimal documentation only.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_agent_long_term_memory
records.scope: README and SQLite experiment
findings: Four distinct SQLite connections verify exact SHA-256 matches for 15 records and retain a state update across connections.
Default corpus is synthetic; historical 15-document result is archival.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_ai_infrastructure_agent
records.scope: README and allowlisted action planner
findings: Planner normalizes commands and performs exact allowlist membership checks.
Every result has executed=false; no shell, host, server or cloud API is called.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_backtest_oos_lab
records.scope: README and leakage demonstration
findings: Code compares lagged signal positions with deliberately same-period lookahead positions.
Fixture is six hand-authored prices; tests demonstrate the lookahead effect.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_benchmark_statistics
records.scope: README, uncertainty analysis, tests and archived result
findings: Archived UCI digits comparison: 450 test rows, three paired seeds; mean FP32 accuracy 95.85%, binary model 88.81%, difference -7.04 percentage points.
Exploratory paired-seed t95 interval approximately -11.98 to -2.09 percentage points.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_cpu_gpu_cost_benchmark
records.scope: README, cost calculator, tests and repository tree
findings: Calculator estimates cost per thousand correct answers from caller-supplied hourly cost, throughput, utilization and success rate.
No live provider tariffs or paid GPU bills; inspected tree exposes no independent GPU harness. README's local CPU measurement claim was not confirmed in inspected source.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_fault_injection_lab
records.scope: README, two-replica experiment, QA validator, evidence scope and results
findings: Two local HTTP server processes; three process terminations per run plus deterministic 503s and delays.
Archived results: no_retry 91/120 successes and retry_failover 120/120 in each of three runs.
QA validator checks six summaries and expected counts.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_rag_quality_cost
records.scope: README, diagnostic function and tests
findings: Function reports required-document recall separately from answer-claim support rate and identifies unsupported claim IDs.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_retry_storm_lab
records.scope: README, policy implementation, tests, benchmark and results card
findings: Circuit breaker uses epoch-tagged permits, one half-open probe and stale-completion fencing; local bulkhead rejection is not recorded as upstream failure.
Tests cover concurrent half-open admission, stale completion, atomic retry budget, deterministic jitter and local-only endpoint restriction.
Benchmark: 240 requests x six policies x three repeats on one localhost service; protected policy success 32.92% vs budget_bulkhead 56.25%.

records.name: timeweb_synergy_service_recovery
records.scope: README, recovery scenario and tests
findings: Inspected article11 is a pure-state simulator and never executes real service or file operations.
Data-loss restore is blocked pending approval; tests assert real_actions_executed=false.
README describes local HTTP/SQLite restarts, but inspected source path does not demonstrate that claim.

records.name: synergy_agi_nexus
records.scope: README, AI proposal contract and contract tests
findings: README defines NEXUS as intelligence engine and explicitly denies automatic financial, ledger, payment, consensus or deployment authority.
ai_proposal_v1 contract requires task type, model ID, confidence and limitations; human authorization defaults true.
Contract tests assert that NEXUS output is a proposal, not authorization.
limitations: README describes target canonical architecture; this review does not prove all listed generations are production-integrated.
No cross-repository runtime call is established by the proposal contract alone.

records.name: synergy_system
records.scope: README governance snapshot, federation config and typed event envelope
findings: README snapshot as of 2026-11-20 lists 77 interface components, 39 contract families, 42 authorities, 44 runtime adapter edges and zero E2E-tested edges.
SynergyEnvelope carries contract ID, event/trace IDs, producer, authority, timestamps, payload digest, evidence IDs, idempotency key and state version; canonical JSON payload SHA-256 is verified.
Federation config explicitly states architecture relation is not runtime dependency and green requires reproducible evidence.
limitations: README owner inventory says 92 and config/repository_federation_v2.yaml says 75 as of 2026-09-28; both are stale relative to current 112-node inventory.
The governance registry is the existing authority; Hypergraph V3 should project/reference it rather than create a competing contract authority.
Zero E2E-tested edges means adapter declarations must not be treated as working integrations.

records.name: synergy_meta_api
records.scope: README, deny-by-default policy and execution API
findings: V0.1 prototype exposes local read-only tools and a subset of MCP initialize/ping/tools/list/tools/call.
Policy denies by default, enforces tenant/tool/scope matching and returns approval_required for allowed mutating actions only when permission is not read-only.
Connector execution is disabled unless SYNERGY_ENABLE_CONNECTOR_CALLS=true; code explicitly says there is no authentication yet and flag is for private development only.
limitations: Not full MCP streaming, sessions, OAuth, A2A, production tenancy or public-safe external execution.
No runtime integration to the 22 proposed routers is proven.

records.name: synergy_net
records.scope: README, transport evidence contract and tests
findings: README describes SynergyNet as a planned network overlay and explicitly frames performance benefits as hypotheses requiring matched benchmarks.
Runtime contract helper hashes delivered content, requires authenticated delivery and validates route endpoints and basic measurement bounds.
Tests validate archive evidence gating, authenticated delivery and content hashing.
limitations: Inspected runtime file is a contract/evidence helper, not a complete P2P transport implementation.
No measured network throughput, latency, multipath, peer discovery or production post-quantum session is established.

records.name: synergy_hierarchical_cognitive_memory_architecture
records.scope: README, dependency AST scanner, cross-repository registry, contract intelligence, tests and security policy
findings: Main branch contains a substantial implementation: SQLite-backed memory, git dependency intelligence, cross-repository inventory and contract intelligence; this contradicts the stale synergy_system README statement that its main branch is README-only.
Dependency scanner parses Python AST at exact commit SHAs and does not import or execute repository code; dynamic dispatch and runtime plugin loading are not inferred.
Cross-repository registry canonicalizes GitHub URLs, derives stable SHA-256 URL identities, records observations and stores explicitly evidenced candidate dependencies only.
Contract intelligence requires full commit SHA, blob SHA, safe source path and explicit declared/upstream contract IDs; ambiguous and unresolved providers are reported instead of guessed.
Security docs keep API local-only, require admin token for system-core endpoint and reserve trust elevation for authorized review.
limitations: Repository identity in its own cross-repo DB is a canonical-URL hash, not GitHub's immutable provider ID; Hypergraph needs a mapping layer.
Static AST links do not prove runtime calls; candidate dependencies do not prove reachability or compatibility.
This review did not execute the test suite or validate current branch CI.

records.name: synergy_agentic_ai_economy
records.scope: README, economy simulation contract, ledger and closed-economy tests
findings: Repository is explicitly a deterministic research/simulation environment; internal issuance, gross TVL and transaction volume are not automatically real profit.
Closed economy engine asserts zero external inflow/outflow, conservation and internal jobs/useful work; internal loans/deposits/investments do not create system cash.
Simulation contract explicitly sets payment_authority=false and accounting_authority=false.
limitations: No live payment execution or real-world marketplace settlement is established by this simulation.
Historical replay includes modeled layers and must retain its own evidence/assumption labels.

records.name: synergy_market_graph
records.scope: README, graph core, fair-value contract, enterprise resilience/auth and tests
findings: Executable edge rate deducts fee and slippage; graph enumerates paths and cycles; fair value is geometric mean of positive executable path rates.
Typed fair-value contract returns authorization=false; tests assert advisory-only output.
Enterprise layer includes HMAC-signed tenant/role token helpers and retry/circuit-breaker primitives.
limitations: Capacity, latency, stale quotes, correlated/overlapping paths and execution sequencing are not incorporated into core fair-value calculation.
Fee/slippage bounds are not enforced in Edge model; negative executable rates are filtered from fair-value paths rather than rejected at ingestion.
A conversion graph is not a general buyer/seller offer marketplace or commercial transaction orchestrator.

records.name: synergy_meta_os
records.scope: README, compatibility orchestrator and orchestrator tests
findings: Runtime verifies manifest shape, service role/capability ceilings, artifact SHA-256 and explicit attestation for high-value roles.
Activation launches subprocesses with reduced environment and POSIX CPU/address-space/open-file limits; audit events are appended to JSONL.
Tests cover manifest verification, dry-run, activation and rejection of capability escalation.
limitations: RLIMITs and process sessions are not an OS sandbox: no namespaces, seccomp, chroot, filesystem policy or network isolation is applied by the inspected code.
This compatibility runtime is not evidence of the full native TURBO Linux ring-3 service-cell implementation.
The test service is a trivial local shell script; production service isolation and rollback semantics are not proven.

records.name: synergy_financial_os
records.scope: README, accounting-recognition contract and contract tests
findings: README defines Financial OS as canonical accounting authority and distinguishes external profit from internal value changes.
Main branch tree contains contract and test artifacts; README says larger runtime is on open feature PRs, so do not treat those unmerged branches as main implementation.
Recognition helper validates SETTLED/reconciled settlement only when settlement_payload is supplied; parameter is optional, so callers can bypass upstream settlement check by omitting it.
Empty entries pass _check_double_entry because zero debits equals zero credits; non-empty journal and nonzero amount invariants are not enforced here.
limitations: Main branch is a contract-level implementation, not the full Financial OS runtime described in README.
Accounting authority does not itself execute payments or prove external settlement.

records.name: synergy_pay_system
records.scope: README, live readiness, execution coordinator, provider registry and settlement engine
findings: Live readiness requires global enablement, production environment, emergency-stop clearance, approved change ticket, notional limit, jurisdiction allowlists and provider allowlist.

Provider profiles model credentials/scopes, legal basis, KYB, settlement accounts, fees, rails, prefunds, HSM/MPC custody, sanctions screening, audits, bridge codehashes, health and disaster recovery.
LiveExecutionCoordinator rejects expired/non-executable quotes, missing provider context, provider policy failures and readiness blockers before calling an authenticated adapter.
README says live execution is disabled by default and public quotes are non-executable until authenticated adapters are separately approved.
limitations: Inspected SettlementEngine stores records and idempotency keys in process memory; this is not durable cross-process exactly-once settlement.
A crash after external provider execution but before ledger posting requires durable outbox/reconciliation evidence beyond the in-memory path inspected.
Source review does not prove access to live bank/CBDC/venue accounts or regulatory authorization.

records.name: synergy_ai_financial_system
records.scope: README, integer graph arbitrage simulator and scenario evidence contract
findings: Graph arbitrage uses integer arithmetic, explicit fee/transfer-tax treatment and USDT cycle repayment; internal token QE is assigned zero external reserve value while paired stablecoin/POL capital is charged to LNAV.
Scenario evidence contract explicitly sets accounting_authority=false, settlement_authority=false and capital_authorization=false.
limitations: The inspected module is a deterministic simulation/research model, not a live exchange executor or accounting/settlement authority.
Deployment claims require archive-block fork tests and external reserve/fee evidence as stated in project docs.

records.name: synergy_riskguard
records.scope: README, risk core, typed risk contract, enterprise service and tests
findings: Core evaluates daily loss, drawdown, historical VaR/CVaR, gross exposure and single-position caps; contract requires upstream validation gate PAPER or CANARY.
Enterprise service verifies HMAC JWT claims, tenant identity and roles, and records audit events.
README reports 21 local tests and 80/80 local health checks; this audit did not rerun them.
limitations: historical_var and cvar return 0.0 when fewer than five returns are supplied; decide may then treat missing/insufficient history as zero market risk instead of failing closed.
Core decide uses abs(order.notional) and does not independently reject negative notional or invalid side; contract adapter checks positive notional, but direct callers can bypass that layer.
Local smoke and benchmarks are not production SLA or realized trading evidence.

records.name: synergy_search_engline
records.scope: README, HardNAV multiplier simulation and assumptions/limits
findings: Despite its name, main branch contains a deterministic HardNAV multiplier simulation and EVM lab baseline, not a general-purpose search engine or web index.
README labels outputs simulated and lists omitted stochastic edge decay, competition, missed fills, gas volatility, MEV distribution, bridge risk and latency.
limitations: Do not assign this repository as the provider for classifieds, bank or real-estate search without separate implementation evidence.

records.name: synergy_lead_search_engline
records.scope: README, SQLite/FTS5 lead store, token-protected API, CRM approval dispatcher and tests
findings: README labels V8 as offline candidate, not deployed lead discovery; scoring is an interpretable regex/rule baseline, not trained CatBoost.
Documents are stored in SQLite/FTS5; candidate signals never equal verified buyer; CRM outbox requires human review, documented lawful basis, contact opt-in and explicit approval.
API fails closed if LEAD_OS_API_TOKEN is missing/short; CRM dispatch requires approved outbox state and HTTPS webhook.
limitations: No tenant_id isolation is present in inspected document/review/outbox schema; single operator token is not a multi-tenant authorization model.
No production deployment, external crawler or upgraded ML ranker is proven.
Configured CRM webhook checks HTTPS but does not enforce a fixed Bitrix24 host allowlist; outbound target is environment-controlled and should be hardened before hosting untrusted tenants.

records.name: synergy_ai_company
records.scope: README and complete repository tree
findings: README explicitly labels the repository STUB/concept; tree contains README, docs and image assets only.
limitations: No autonomous company runtime, agent role engine, process execution or integration is established.

records.name: synergy_maps
records.scope: README, EAEU country registry and Overture tile coverage auditor
findings: Main branch has a CesiumJS global globe and EAEU country boundary subset, with country IDs and geometry validation tests.

Overture coverage auditor verifies raw tile artifact hashes, pinned release and run ledger; its output explicitly does not claim geographic completeness, authoritative borders, cross-tile deduplication or 3D Tiles publication.
limitations: Not a detailed worldwide street/cadastral/3D map; higher-resolution L1-L4 layers remain planned or require external datasets.
No verified live integration with logistics, real-estate or enterprise routers was found in the inspected files.

records.name: synergy_agi_autopilot
records.scope: README and complete main-branch tree
findings: README explicitly labels main as STUB/architecture node; repository tree contains README, docs and assets only.
limitations: No DAG planner, agent runtime, execution engine or integration is implemented on main.

records.name: synergy_ai_coder
records.scope: README, engineering evidence contract and tests
findings: Compact evidence-contract layer maps REQ requirements to affected repositories and changes; APPROVED requires all checks PASS.
Optional SHA-256 hashes bind evidence bytes and artifact bytes; README correctly says hash is content identity, not proof of correctness.
limitations: This is not a complete autonomous coding agent, code execution environment or repository orchestration runtime.
Commit SHA validation checks format only; it does not fetch/verify that commit exists in the named repository.

records.name: synergy_ai_workspace
records.scope: main README plus release/v1.0-desktop-rc local service, orchestrator and capital engine
findings: Default main contains only README; inspected application code is on release/v1.0-desktop-rc, not main.
Release branch service binds local control plane to 127.0.0.1:8129, stores tasks/leads/actions/audit in SQLite WAL and requires bearer token.
Workspace orchestrator exposes only local read/planning capabilities; external Avito publishing and investment trading are blocked and it returns external_effects=false.
Capital engine stores source-supplied financial records with immutable source IDs and SHA-256 conflict detection; it explicitly does not call banks, brokers or exchanges.
limitations: Release branch README says Windows installer and GUI E2E are not confirmed; not a production desktop release.
No tenant separation in the inspected local schema; not a public multi-tenant SaaS backend.
Main branch is README-only; branch code must not be described as merged main functionality.

records.name: synergy_messenger
records.scope: README, package manifest and complete main-branch tree
findings: README describes Messenger V3 alpha architecture and explicitly says production security, real MLS backend and physical-device tests remain required.
Main tree contains README, package.json, service worker and documentation/assets, but no application source or tests/v3 files.
package.json test script references tests/v3/*.test.js and build:www references scripts/copy-www.js; these paths are absent from inspected main tree.
limitations: Main branch does not substantiate the claimed messenger runtime; branch/tag code must be separately audited before reuse.
No cryptographic implementation or P2P messaging behavior is verified by this main-branch snapshot.

records.name: synergy_algotrading_graph_system
records.scope: README and complete main-branch tree
findings: README describes a formal research architecture for amount-dependent market graphs, shared capacity and settlement-aware routing.
Main tree contains README and assets only; no graph algorithm, package, tests or settlement evidence ledger is implemented.
limitations: Do not treat the architecture specification as an executable arbitrage engine.

records.name: synergy_relative_value
records.scope: README, OLS pair core and non-authorizing signal contract
findings: Core fits a linear pair by least squares, computes spread z-score and a normalized carry heuristic.
Contract outputs authorization=false and requires downstream domain validation.
limitations: OLS fit and high z-score do not establish cointegration, stationarity or stable hedge ratio; README explicitly lists these missing tests.
No costs, borrow/funding, liquidity, asynchronous price or selection-bias model in the core.

records.name: synergy_adaptive_engine
records.scope: README, adaptive ensemble core and market-regime contract
findings: AdaptiveEnsemble updates strategy weights using exponentiated clipped rewards and caps per-step weight movement.
Regime classifier returns UNKNOWN with fewer than five returns and emits a non-authorizing market-regime contract.
README documents tenant-aware RBAC, audit events and live execution disabled by default.
limitations: No out-of-sample or live trading validation was executed in this review.
Core input validation for finite rewards/threshold ordering should be strengthened before adversarial or production use.

records.name: synergy_midas_institutional
records.scope: README, bounded assessment core, contract and tests
findings: MidasOrchestrator calls injected validator and risk functions; it blocks on failed validation or non-positive risk and caps approved notional at target notional.
Contract binds decision to the exact signal and emits authorization=false plus requires_canonical_risk_validation=true.
README explicitly states EXECUTION_READY is only readiness for the next gate, not broker authorization.
limitations: Quality and provenance of injected validator/risk functions are outside this repository's core.
The institutional assessment is not itself a canonical risk veto or execution adapter.

records.name: sinergy_super_app
records.scope: README, mobile PWA shell, source-surface integrity contract and Android build workflow
findings: Main contains responsive mobile/PWA HTML, web manifest, Android wrapper and a workflow configured to build assembleDebug.
Surface contract hashes manifest/index/Gradle/wrapper but explicitly sets android_artifact_built=false and deployment_authority=false.
limitations: UI description names wallet, AGI, DAO, L1, MetaPay and mesh modules, but the inspected source-surface contract does not prove these backend integrations exist.
Workflow definition is not proof of a successful APK build or published app.

records.name: sinergy_app
records.scope: README and complete main-branch tree
findings: README states main contains only README.md and explicitly marks the client app STUB/documentation-only.
limitations: No UI source, package/build manifest, tests, CI, release pipeline or API client exists in main.

records.name: synergy_app
records.scope: README, mobile release contract and Android manifest
findings: Main contains Android project, iOS project, web assets, tests/scripts and a source-integrity contract.
Release contract hashes Android Gradle/manifest and iOS project/privacy manifest, checks target/compile SDK 36, cleartext disabled, backups disabled and rejects selected dangerous permissions.
Manifest inspection shows INTERNET only, allowBackup=false, usesCleartextTraffic=false and explicit network security config.
limitations: Source verification does not prove a built, signed or store-published artifact; README explicitly separates these states.
Main branch includes binary finance-next source parts whose full provenance/build integration needs separate audit.

records.name: synergy_apps
records.scope: README, read-only accounting/trust projections and tests
findings: README labels repository an architectural master/documentation layer, not a unified app runtime.
Read models project accounting recognition and blockchain trust status while explicitly returning read_only=true and authority labels canonical_accounting/blockchain_trust.
Tests assert read-only projections.
limitations: Projection helpers do not authenticate source evidence, validate accounting signatures or grant authority; they rely on upstream domain payloads.
Not a marketplace backend or shared app execution runtime.

records.name: synergy_chain
records.scope: README, packaged source boundary, QE V10 Solidity contracts and Foundry tests
findings: Repository separates Node/web source archive, static GitHub Pages subset and QE V10 Solidity testbed as distinct evidence surfaces.
CI defines Node source validation and Foundry build/test; Pages deploys only the static public subset.
QE V10 tests use minimal custom test tokens, fixed DEX and local vault/debt contracts; tests assert NAV conservation and modeled fee loss.
limitations: Source archive is not expanded in the repository; reproducibility depends on archive integrity and its internal lock/dependencies.
QE V10 custom tokens and bridge contracts are research fixtures, not production ERC20/bridge contracts.
Pages deployment cannot run backend sessions, CRM writes, vault or live model calls.

records.name: synergy_metachain
records.scope: README, trust/replay consumer and tests
findings: Consumer requires FINALIZED status, commitment ID, 64-hex payload digest, source event and source contract IDs; repeated commitment IDs in the same process are rejected.
Output explicitly sets claimable_once=true and accounting_authority=false.
limitations: Replay state is an in-memory Python set and is lost on process restart; replay can be accepted after restart unless a durable store is added.
The consumer trusts the supplied FINALIZED flag and digest; it does not verify signatures, chain RPC, light-client proofs, validator set, Merkle/SPV proofs or reorgs.
This is a local trust/replay gate, not a full cross-chain bridge.

records.name: synergy_usds
records.scope: README, explicit security blocker, gitignore and deployment script; secret file contents deliberately not inspected
findings: Repository contains a dedicated SECURITY_FEDERATION_BLOCKER.md that says it is not eligible for runtime federation until deployer credential hygiene is completed.

Tracked root artifact named base-mainnet-deployer.key is present in the Git tree; contents were not inspected. The blocker explicitly says treat it as exposed until proven otherwise and rotate/revoke.
The deploy script expects a private key file, checks Base chain ID 8453 and a 0600 permission mode before deploying; this does not neutralize a tracked root credential.
limitations: Keep ARCHITECTURAL_ONLY and block deployment/federation until rotation, history cleanup, secret scanning and independent verification are complete.
Economic model's external value-added assumption is scenario input, not profit generated by mint/sell mechanics.

records.name: synergy_cashero
records.scope: README, repository tree and CASRSv3/CASRGv3 Solidity token/collateral contracts; secret files not opened
findings: Main contains CASRSv3/CASRGv3 contracts, CPMM robot/simulation scripts and archived 150-cycle reports.
README explicitly warns that synthetic pool returns are not externally realized income and tracked configuration files may contain secrets.
Git tree contains tracked .env, owner.env, bot1.env and bot2.env files; their contents were not inspected. No .gitignore file was found at the expected root path.
limitations: Treat any credentials in tracked environment files as exposed until proven otherwise; rotate/revoke and purge history if real secrets are present.
Custom token contracts and bot simulations require independent security review, fork-state evidence and reserve accounting before mainnet claims.
No external audit or verified live settlement evidence was established by this review.

records.name: synergy_turbo_linux
records.scope: README, Turbo Core capability/scheduler/IPC implementation and historical SSH key incident report
findings: Turbo Core implements keyed SipHash capability seals, rights masks, a 64-priority bitmap scheduler and cacheline-separated SPSC ring.

Historical security incident report confirms an unencrypted SSH private key was committed to main history on 2026-09-04; current tree removed the private file, but external key rotation/revocation and history sanitization are explicitly not proven.
Scheduler enqueue does not track whether task_id is already queued; enqueueing the same ID twice can create a self-referential next pointer and leave the queue stuck.
limitations: Microbenchmarks are not OS-wide acceleration claims; remote orchestration is a separate historical track.
Capability generation is MAC-bound but inspected resolve path does not consult a revocation/current-generation registry.
Old SSH credential must remain treated as compromised until revoked at every authorized host.

records.name: synergy_computing_topology
records.scope: README, V4 correctness harness, archived gate results and validation report
findings: V4 harness compares batch and sequential QPIPE, checks deterministic repeated runs, 1000 fresh-process decompression corpora with SHA-256, corruption rejection, cache restart/delete and tail-byte preservation.
Archived 2026-09-30 gate results report the userspace checks passing and kernel runtime NOT TESTED due vermagic mismatch (built for 6.12.96 headers, host kernel 6.18.44).
Measured speedups are specific to repeated queries over a precomputed compact descriptor index with build cost included; one-query case is 0.931x, while 3000 varied queries report 2116.714x.
limitations: These are archived results, not tests rerun in this audit session.
No OS-wide, arbitrary-workload or production kernel performance claim is supported.
Kernel module runtime on the current host was explicitly not tested.

records.name: synergy_motherboard_xpu_xml
records.scope: README, analytical XPU model and deterministic EML Q16.16 reference evaluator
findings: Repository provides explicit first-order compute, HBM, PCIe, persistent-memory, area and energy models with coefficients labeled as assumptions unless measured.
EML Q16.16 reference evaluator uses Decimal exp/ln and enforces b>0 plus signed 32-bit input range.
README explicitly disclaims fabricated EML cell, timing-closed RTL, measured silicon area/energy and CPU/GPU replacement equivalence.
limitations: No fabricated silicon, FPGA timing closure, synthesized area/energy or production hardware benchmark is established.
7.077888 T EML primitives/s is an analytical ceiling under modeled assumptions, not FLOPS or measured throughput.

records.name: synergy_long_term_harness
records.scope: README and complete main-branch tree
findings: Main branch contains only a one-line README heading; no harness, test runner, long-term soak orchestration or artifacts.
limitations: Cannot be treated as the federation-wide long-term test harness until implementation exists.

records.name: synergy_quantlab
records.scope: README, purged walk-forward core and validation decision contract
findings: Core provides expanding walk-forward folds with purge/embargo, return metrics, simple linear cost adjustment and RESEARCH/PAPER/CANARY gate; it never returns FULL_PRODUCTION.
Validation contract binds candidate event ID, protocol ID and optional dataset manifest digest; it is non-execution authority.
limitations: Sharpe uses simple sample standard deviation without autocorrelation/Newey-West correction; no probabilistic Sharpe, multiple-testing correction, bootstrap CI or nonlinear impact model.
Dataset manifest digest is optional and the inspected contract does not verify its format or fetch the dataset itself.
No tests were executed during this audit; README's local test status remains documentary evidence.

records.name: synergy_midas_ai
records.scope: README, portfolio decision contract and M4 market advisory consumers
findings: README declares MIDAS AI as target canonical home for independently validated trading architecture and explicitly preserves historical repositories as provenance.
Main tree contains contract files and research artifacts, but no general strategy-engine Python package under src; this is a contract/target-architecture layer, not a complete live trading engine.
Portfolio decision contract validates confidence, position side and non-negative notional; M4 advisory consumers explicitly return authorization=false and require domain validation.
limitations: Canonical-home status is a target ownership decision, not proof that all strategy experts, data pipelines and execution adapters are consolidated.
No direct broker execution or canonical accounting authority is implemented in the inspected main branch.

records.name: synergy_market_maker
records.scope: README, quote core and non-authorizing liquidity quote contract
findings: Core computes bid/ask/reservation from mid, inventory, volatility and configured spread/risk parameters; inventory limit returns no quote.
Contract includes observation ID and explicit authorization=false; enterprise tests described in README cover trader/viewer roles and audit linkage.
limitations: No order-book depth, queue position, adverse selection, fill probability, venue latency, cancel/replace, multi-venue inventory or realized maker P&L in the core.
MMConfig has no explicit parameter validation for gamma/kappa/horizon/max_inventory/min spread; malformed config can produce invalid geometry or math errors.
Quote and hedge notional are proposals, not orders or fills.

records.name: synergy_marketvision
records.scope: README, OHLCV feature cube and market-features contract
findings: Core converts OHLCV windows into a 3×window×4 float32 cube using returns, high-low spread, log-volume and direction with median/IQR scaling.
Federation contract emits only shape/mean/std/energy summary and explicit authorization=false.
limitations: Feature cube is not a forecast or trading signal; it excludes order book, bid/ask and cross-asset context.
Scaling occurs within the current window and the summary compresses the tensor heavily; downstream OOS ablation is required to prove value.

records.name: synergy_midas_ai_trading_system
records.scope: README critical findings, decision pipeline, risk engine, API/WebSocket, MT5 simulator, signal fusion and archive service
findings: DecisionPipeline.run_with_metrics risk-veto branch references undefined exc and uses bare raise outside an active except; veto can crash instead of returning a safe blocked decision.
RiskEngine stores lower-tail return quantiles as negative VaR/CVaR while is_veto compares them against positive maximum thresholds; sign convention is inconsistent.
WebSocket /logs/stream and /metrics/stream call accept without require_api_key; HTTP endpoints are protected.
MT5Execution.execute performs local parameter/slippage/latency checks and returns accepted without calling mt5.order_send; accepted is not submitted or filled.
ArchiveService chain_hash previous state is held in an instance-local dictionary and is not recovered from persistent archive on restart.
limitations: README lists these as P0/P1 findings; this review confirmed the relevant source paths but did not run the test suite.
Legacy scripts coexist with modular package; authority path and historical code still require isolation.
No live broker execution or independent audited PnL is established by this main-branch package.

records.name: midas_lite
records.scope: README, legacy MT5 agent source and sealed EURUSD H1 research evidence
findings: Repository preserves a EURUSD H1 specialist with frozen configuration and separate rolling and sealed OOS reports.

README explicitly labels 100-window/415-signal/688 gross pips as modeled research, and a separate sealed 2-month period as four trades, three correct directions and -3.5 net pips at assumed 0.5 pip cost.
Legacy agi_trader_final_v1.py contains direct MetaTrader5 order_send calls at multiple code paths.
limitations: The presence of order_send means the legacy script can attempt real broker orders depending on terminal/account configuration; do not run outside isolated demo until all paths are audited and execution is explicitly disabled by default.
No broker-confirmed PnL or live MT5 test is established by the README's research reports.
Legacy and specialist lines should be isolated; research reports are not permission to execute.

records.name: synergy_ai_trade_terminal
records.scope: README, Cassandra terminal source and process supervisor
findings: README explicitly states credentials are embedded in Python source and must be revoked/replaced before public deployment.

Credential-pattern scan confirmed hard-coded password/account credential fields and bearer-token handling in cassandra_v6_FIXED.py; token material is also emitted into a login_success event/log prefix.
Repository includes a separate order tester with broker requests and stop-limit management; this audit did not execute any order path.
limitations: Treat embedded credentials and issued tokens as exposed; rotate/revoke them and remove sensitive history after rotation.
No evidence of tenant isolation or production-grade secret management was established.
Order execution paths require separate authorization, demo-only testing and explicit operator confirmation.

records.name: quantum-trading_metatrader5
records.scope: README and MT5/Qiskit main program
findings: README and main show price_binary is passed into analyze_market_state but not used; circuit parameters are fixed and do not depend on market history.
The code compares stochastic Aer measurements with future horizon labels; it does not establish predictive accuracy or quantum advantage.
Main contains MT5 initialization/data collection but no order_send path in the inspected file.
limitations: Research prototype only; no proof of QPE correctness, market forecast skill or quantum advantage.
No live trading execution was found in the inspected main.py; other files were not exhaustively audited.

records.name: synergy_ai_language
records.scope: README, requirement-to-change trace, source-indexed agent, compiler, command runner and tests
findings: SemanticTrace creates REQ-linked intent/repository/change/impact graphs and records tool actions; AST extraction is bounded and does not execute source.
Workspace file APIs restrict paths to workspace and hide common secret-like filenames; run_command blocks shell operators and selected destructive shells/commands.

Compiler emits Python/C/Rust/Solidity/Kotlin from instruction strings; Python uses repr, but C/Rust/Solidity/Kotlin generators interpolate action/target directly into string literals without language-specific escaping.
execute_python_file and Workspace.run_command use subprocess with no OS sandbox, namespace, filesystem isolation or network egress control; approval and command filters are not a sandbox.
SemanticTrace.record truncates the first output line but does not redact credential patterns, despite its docstring saying raw credentials are not persisted.
limitations: No target-language compilation or sandboxed execution is demonstrated for generated C/Rust/Solidity/Kotlin.
Auto-approval bypasses interactive approval; commands run with the user's OS permissions after filtering.
File-name secret filters do not identify arbitrary secrets embedded in ordinary config/source files.

records.name: synergy_gllm_nexus
records.scope: unified-v3-generalization-first branch README, graph-native runtime, MoE router and frozen benchmark artifacts; main is docs/registry only
findings: Default main branch is documentation/benchmark registry; substantive Python runtime is on unified-v3-generalization-first at commit a18fa5a (2026-09-20).

Branch runtime has typed GraphCard/TypedHyperEdge, persistent DynamicHyperGraph, mutation/retraction, temporal/causal reasoning, graph recurrent core, Russian neural compiler and AnswerGraph semantic guard.

NEXUS-MOE-B1 archived one-shot result reports learned MoE 94.44%, best single 33.33%, naive 59.17%, oracle 95.83%; negative transfer 1.45%. Result file says sealed_before_evaluation=true and test_open_count=1.
FTX1 README says exact BLIND generator/corpus/gold are sealed outside development branch and should be opened exactly once after preblind freeze.
limitations: Runtime is not in default main; branch is dated 2026-09-20 and must be explicitly pinned before use.
Benchmark results are synthetic/frozen protocol results, not real-world general intelligence or production performance.
FTX1 sealed blind contents were not accessed; no claim about its final score is made.
The graph-native runtime is a distinct cognitive hypergraph, not a substitute for the repository-dependency/evidence graph.

records.name: synergy_ai_llm_rwkv
records.scope: feature/rwkv7-original-weights branch quantizer, Triton low-bit matvec, evaluation harness and tests; main contains workflow/docs
findings: Default main does not contain the quantizer/runtime; experimental implementation is on feature/rwkv7-original-weights at commit dfc163f.
Quantizer preserves tensor names/shapes and samples weight reconstruction MSE; README explicitly says this is not activation/task-loss sensitivity and full 2.9B checkpoint has not been validated.
Triton backend implements one-CTA-per-row matvec, rejects N>65536, and is not a full RWKV generation runtime.
Tests cover synthetic arrays and a tiny synthetic checkpoint pipeline; no real checkpoint, full-model perplexity or target-GPU performance was measured.
limitations: The 700 MB target is a disk archive budget; restored FP16 checkpoint expands and requires original RWKV runner.
Full model quality parity, long-context drift and speed are unmeasured; quantization can degrade quality, especially 1-bit.
Branch implementation is experimental and not in default main.

records.name: synergy_matrix_sota

records.name: synegy_ai_compress
records.scope: README, extended benchmark artifacts, environment metadata and source_snapshot gitlink; no engine source inspected
findings: Main branch contains benchmark reports/results and a source_snapshot gitlink (commit 6d2d8f0c...) rather than directly vendored engine source.
No .gitmodules file was found, so the source_snapshot submodule URL is not declared in the repository metadata inspected.
README distinguishes fresh 38-profile results from historical/legacy comparisons and labels the benchmark environment and dataset limitations.
limitations: The compression engine implementation cannot be independently rebuilt from this repository alone until the submodule URL and exact source are available.
Benchmark score tables are not proof of general compression superiority; workload, quality, compute and full amortized model costs must be compared.

records.name: synergy_qr_compress
records.scope: README, QTC2/QTD3 codec, container, round-trip and exact shared-dictionary tests
findings: QTC2 stores a model ID and timestamp-addressed shared dictionary reference; exact mode can have zero residual bytes when the target is already present in the shared model.
Patch mode stores changed bytes and original SHA-256; decoder rejects wrong model IDs and corrupted payloads.
Tests use random data and a shared model; one-byte mutation on a 1,000,000-byte target verifies exact reconstruction and 99.9999% model coverage.
limitations: Zero residual does not mean zero total storage: dictionary/model bytes must exist and be available to the decoder; amortized cost across all consumers is the meaningful metric.
This is shared-model temporal storage/reference coding, not standalone general-purpose lossless compression for unrelated files.
Benchmark's random base and one-byte mutation are synthetic; no broad corpus or full storage economics study is established.

records.name: synergy_nexus_science_agent

The split helper defaults purge_bars and embargo_bars to zero; callers must supply purge at least as large as the longest label horizon, so a default call does not itself guarantee leakage-safe folds.

records.name: synergy_project

Decimal amounts are not checked with is_finite(); Decimal('Infinity') can pass positive capital/max_amount checks. Contract functions construct payloads only and do not provide durable approval workflow or payment execution.

records.name: synergy_trademux

The benchmark payload contract checks dimensions and candidate counts but does not reject non-finite elapsed_s; NaN compares false to <0 and can be serialized as a MEASURED benchmark unless the caller rejects it.

records.name: cross_forex_arbitrage_trading_metatrader_5
records.scope: README plus main source file review; no backtest or live execution performed.
findings: Source creates synthetic prices from same-day M1 bars and derives direction from the mean spread across the entire day before simulating a trade from the day's data; this introduces look-ahead in the daily backtest.
TP/SL pip conversion uses a fixed 0.00001 price multiplier; JPY and broker-specific digits/tick sizes are not handled.
Historical bid/ask are fabricated from close with a fixed 0.1-pip spread; this is not executable cross-rate arbitrage evidence.

records.name: computer_vision_trading_metatrader_5
records.scope: README plus main source file review; no backtest or live execution performed.
findings: Source builds rolling 60-bar windows with 24-bar forward targets and chronological 80/20 train/test split.
The train/validation split then uses shuffle=True on overlapping windows, so adjacent windows with heavily shared history/targets can leak across train and validation.
README itself lists purged walk-forward splitting, window isolation, and independent security/engineering audit as unresolved; no trading profitability or deployment evidence is established.

records.name: swap_arbitrage_metatrader_5
records.scope: README plus main source file review; no backtest or live execution performed.
findings: Source uses current broker swap_long/swap_short metadata alongside historical price returns; it does not demonstrate a historical daily swap-rate series for the full 2015-2025 simulation horizon.
README explicitly says spread, commissions, slippage, margin and stop-out are absent, no reproducible ten-year historical-swap backtest is proven, and dependencies are not pinned.
SLSQP optimization and three equity simulations are quantitative research only, not evidence of executable positive carry arbitrage.

records.name: shtenco_multi_threaded_trading_robot_with_machine_learning_python
records.scope: README plus main source file review; no backtest or live execution performed.
findings: Source contains a direct live mt5.order_send path and retries each request up to 30,000 times with 3-second sleeps; repeated sends can create duplicate orders if a broker response is delayed or ambiguous.
Symbol workers can operate concurrently without a single serialized order/risk arbiter; global position flags and portfolio exposure are race-prone.
Risk sizing uses stop_loss_pips * trade_tick_value without trade_tick_size conversion, and forces broker minimum lot even when it exceeds the calculated risk budget.

process_data performs markup, GMM clustering and RFECV before chronological train/test separation; online_trading also consumes previously prepared test_features rather than a fresh last-bar inference path.

records.name: global_liquidity_dataminer
records.scope: README plus main source file review; no backtest or live execution performed.
findings: Source labels yfinance FX-price proxies (EURGBP, USDJPY, USDCNY scaled by constants) as ECB/BOJ/PBOC balance-sheet series; these are not central-bank balance-sheet observations.
Forecast confidence is clipped test R² in [0,1], not a calibrated probability of forecast correctness.
README identifies missing vintage-aware release-time data; historical macro revisions can leak future information even with chronological price splits.

records.name: 3D_bars_market_structure
records.scope: README plus main source/tests or complete main tree; no tests or backtests executed during this audit.
findings: Source computes Renko-like derived features and interactive plots from MT5 bars; README says there is no dedicated unit-test suite or reproducible out-of-sample evaluation.
Inside the row loop, MinMaxScaler.fit_transform is called on a single time_numeric scalar, which maps each single-value sample to the lower feature bound and collapses that feature to a constant.
The source header states both CC BY-NC-ND and MIT, creating a material licensing conflict that must be resolved before commercial reuse.

records.name: synergy_epstein_network
records.scope: README plus main source/tests or complete main tree; no tests or backtests executed during this audit.
findings: Main contains source adapters, normalization, entity resolution, graph build and tests; README limits the graph to public-source provenance and explicitly denies authority to infer wrongdoing or identity claims.

Exact normalized/token-order name matches are automatically mapped to a canonical person ID without corroborating attributes; identical names can refer to different individuals, so automatic identity merge can create false links. Fuzzy matches are only emitted as review candidates.

Email/phone identifiers are normalized and hashed with unsalted deterministic SHA-256 prefixes; these hashes are pseudonymous identifiers, not anonymization, and can be dictionary-matched. Public-source provenance, minimization, access control and retention remain necessary.

The repository is a research specification, not a deployed monetary protocol or production system.

Archive workflow downloads a Google Drive ZIP, checks exact byte size and ZIP integrity, then computes SHA-256 and splits it into artifacts; no pre-pinned expected archive SHA is compared before processing.
Artifact retention is one day, so this is a transient distribution workflow rather than durable data archival.

records.name: shtenco.github.io
records.scope: README plus selected main-branch source/workflow files; no browser or deployment tests executed during this audit.
findings: Main is a Jekyll/Liquid static portfolio that composes original-source.html with an eight-group JSON catalogue; it is a presentation layer, not a backend or independent certification of every linked project.

The 77-project catalogue is a curated editorial subset, not a claim that the owner has only 77 repositories; README explicitly distinguishes it from the current 86-repository snapshot used by that site's own review.
The _data and data directory tree hashes match in the inspected commit, so the mirrored JSON groups are identical at this snapshot; future drift remains a maintenance risk.

records.name: synergy_shttps
records.scope: README plus selected source/tests on open PR branch; main remains documentation-only.
findings: Main remains specification-only; substantial SHTTPS v2/STCP/Remote MCP implementation and 14 test modules exist on open PR #2 branch feat/stcp-shttps-remote-mcp-v2-20260925.
PQ production provider is an optional liboqs adapter; handshake tests use FakePQProvider, so those tests do not validate the real ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA provider or interoperability.

RemoteMCPGateway.run accepts allowlisted executable basenames including python/cargo/rustc/git, but permits arbitrary arguments such as python -c and does not sandbox the subprocess; basename matching also allows a different executable path ending in an allowed name. It is privileged remote code execution, not a safe command sandbox.

records.name: synergy_agent_long_term_memory
records.scope: README plus selected source/tests on open PR branch; main remains documentation-only.
findings: Main is README-only; the open PR #2 branch feat/persistent-mission-runtime-v1 contains a SQLite WAL/FULL mission journal, checkpoints, idempotency fingerprints, namespace-scoped queries and a bounded ring buffer.
Canonical JSON rejects NaN and custom objects; writes use SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE and idempotency key conflicts reject payload changes.

The runtime explicitly delegates principal authentication and namespace authorization to callers; no LLM provider, task DAG scheduler, cross-repository transaction coordinator or production tenant identity service is included.

records.name: synergy_post_quantum_radio
records.scope: README plus selected source/tests on open PR branch; main remains documentation-only.
findings: Main is documentation-only; open PR #1 branch contains Rust ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87, SLH-DSA-SHAKE-256s, authenticated handshake, replay protections and simulation/hardware backend interfaces.
README explicitly labels the project PROTOTYPE / RESEARCH, states no independent cryptographic audit and rejects the legacy Hash16D 2^4096 security claim.

AttestedHardwareTeleportationBackend accepts a driver-supplied nonzero hardware_attestation_root; may_strengthen_physical_security_claim checks only Hardware mode plus presence. The test's FakeHardware returns [7;32] and is accepted, so no cryptographic signature/attestation-chain verification is implemented at this boundary.
All teleportation correctness tests use a simulator or fake hardware driver; no real QPU/radio hardware experiment is evidenced.
